name: PHUL (Power Hypertrophy Upper Lower)
author: Brandon Campbell (Muscle & Strength)
summary: A 4-day upper/lower split with one heavy power day (3-5 reps on the main lifts) and one higher-rep hypertrophy day (8-15 reps) for each half of the body every week. It is built around the basic barbell lifts plus isolation work.
evidenceNote: At 3-4 sets per exercise, chest and back get about 12-16 weekly sets and quads more, trained twice a week with 1 rep in reserve, which fits current hypertrophy evidence. Weak points: the article gives no load-progression or deload rule, hamstrings get comparatively little direct work, and seven 3-4-set exercises often take longer than the stated 45-60 min.

sources.title: Power Hypertrophy Upper Lower (P.H.U.L.) Workout (Muscle & Strength, updated May 2021)
Wayback Machine snapshot of the same article, 12 Aug 2026 (live site blocks automated access)

schedule: Day 1 Upper Power, Day 2 Lower Power, Day 3 Off, Day 4 Upper Hypertrophy, Day 5 Lower Hypertrophy, Days 6-7 Off. Ab work can be done at the end of training or on off days. Listed time per workout: 45-60 minutes.

progression.description: Article by Brandon Campbell, published 15 Feb 2013, updated 26 May 2021. The author gives no numeric progression rule. His stated rules: all sets end with at least 1 rep left in the tank (struggle on heavy sets but still hit goal reps); start with lower total volume until you adapt; keep the main compounds unchanged but swap other exercises for similar ones if desired. No rest periods are given in the article; Muscle & Strength staff replies in the comments are inconsistent (one suggests 1-2 min between sets, another 2-3 min), and they are not the author text. A staff comment reply (Dec 2024, not the author) suggests adding weight once you reach the top of the set and rep range, e.g. bench 4 x 5. App default: add load when all prescribed sets hit the top of the rep range with 1 rep in reserve.
